title: Smooth queue harmonic throttling to reduce starvation and timeout jitter in continuous batcher
author: Asha Khandelwal
release_notes: Add smooth harmonic throttling and soft-reserve gradient to continuous batcher scheduler; reduces starvation and timeout jitter for mixed KV-heavy workloads. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Background and motivation: In production, continuous batching faces two correlated issues for mixed workloads: 1) short, KV-heavy requests can cause starvation of longer, compute-bound requests when admission is strictly bucketed; 2) timeout jitter arises from abrupt reservation flips and probe retries. This PR introduces a smooth (harmonic) throttling controller and a soft-reserve gradient for the continuous batcher scheduler to reduce both starvation and observed timeout jitter.

Design summary:
- Harmonic throttling: rather than binary reserve/no-reserve thresholds per priority class we compute a harmonic attenuation factor over recent slot consumption and request age distribution. This reduces cliff effects and permits gradual ramp-down under pressure.
- Soft-reserve gradient: existing hard slot reservations were decayed stepwise in backoff; the new gradient decays reservation weight continuously based on moving-average queue occupancy and observed KV pin rates.
- Timeout backoff jitter smoothing: replace exponential jitter seeds with a deterministic jitter window scaled by harmonic factor to avoid synchronized retries during transient overload.
- Priority aging tweak: introduce an age-correction multiplier applied during harmonic attenuation so very old requests get amplified admission probability without bypassing latency SLAs for interactive traffic.

Implementation notes:
- Core scheduler changes in scheduler/continuous/*: added harmonic_controller.{cc,h} and soft_reserve.{cc,h}.
- Metrics: new counters and histograms added under metrics/batcher.h: batch_harmonic_factor, soft_reserve_weight, jitter_window_ms.
- Config knobs (console and runtime flags): continuous.batcher.harmonic_alpha, continuous.batcher.soft_reserve_min, continuous.batcher.jitter_scale.
- Backwards compatible defaults chosen to preserve current steady-state behavior.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for harmonic attenuation math and edge cases
- [x] Integration test that simulates KV heavy short requests vs. long compute requests
- [x] Bench harness run against perf-canary topologies
- [x] Added metrics and console knobs
- [x] Feature flagged behind continuous.batcher.harmonic_enable

Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag. Canary on eu-west-1 first (low traffic) -> us-west-2 perf canaries -> 10% of production traffic with fast rollback if tail latency regresses.

Observed perf numbers (canary):
- KV-dominant 75% short / 25% long mix: p95 latency of long requests decreased by 22% (from 348ms to 272ms)
- Overall token cost: +0.6% (due to slight extra batching overhead for smoothing)
- Timeout error rate: decreased from 0.9% to 0.15%
- p99 latency for short requests: stable within 4%

Implementation commits (high-level):
- feat(scheduler): add harmonic_controller and integrate into admission path
- perf(batcher): implement soft-reserve gradient and metrics
- test(batcher): add mixed workload integration test
- tools: add canary harness config and dashboard panels
- docs: runtime knobs and rollout guide

Changed areas (high-level):
- scheduler/continuous/harmonic_controller.cc/h
- scheduler/continuous/soft_reserve.cc/h
- scheduler/continuous/admission_path.cc (integration points)
- metrics/batcher.h + metrics/registry changes
- config/runtime_defaults.yaml (new knobs)
- tests/integration/batcher_mixed_workload_test.cc

Review summary and conversation:
- Liam O'Rourke: "Nice approach; can you show expected behavior when harmonic_alpha -> 0 (degenerate case)?"
- Author (Asha): "When harmonic_alpha approaches 0 the controller becomes conservative and reverts towards current hard-reserve behaviour; added unit test for alpha=0 in harmonic_controller_test."
- Nina Patel: "We should be careful about the jitter window impacting streaming latency; please add a canary with streaming enabled."
- Author: "Added canary run with streaming flag; metric shows streaming p95 unchanged within noise floor."
- Marcus Green: "Minor: rename soft_reserve_min -> soft_reserve_floor for clarity."
- Author: "Done in follow-up commit, updated docs."

CI / checks:
- unit tests: pass
- integration (mixed-workload): pass
- lint: pass
- perf-canary-run: pass

Merge outcome: merged via squash (squash and merge) with commit message summarizing the approach and referencing ENG-4128.

Rollback instructions: flip continuous.batcher.harmonic_enable=false and soft_reserve_min=0 to return to prior reservation behavior; alert runbook added to SRE handbook.

Notes/risks:
- The harmonic attenuation introduces additional CPU work in the hot admission path; measured overhead ~0.9% CPU at max load and was judged acceptable.
- Edge-case: extremely bursty KV patterns can transiently increase token cost due to extra small batches; mitigation via auto-tuning of harmonic_alpha in a follow-up.

Related work: inspired by adaptive admission controllers in earlier PRs but focuses on smoothing rather than strict slot reallocation.
